newsitem.title: LIBERIA: SOCCER-LATE DEAL SAVES LIBERIA-ZAIRE NATIONS' CUP GAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE DEAL SAVES LIBERIA-ZAIRE NATIONS' CUP GAME.

text.p: Liberia's cash-strapped soccer squad flew out on Saturday for an African Nations' Cup qualifier in Zaire after negotiating a last-minute deal over the cost of the trip.

The home-based players left on a private charter to the Ivory Coast where world footballer of the year George Weah and other exiles were due to join them for the trip to Kinshasa for Sunday's group six game.

Officials had said lack of money threatened to sideline the war-ravaged West African nation from the competition. But the acting chairman of the interim ruling State Council ordered finance ministry officials to find the necessary funds.

Weah, with AC Milan, paid $40,000 of his own money to fund Liberia's last two qualifying matches against Gambia. But he said last month that he could not continue to underwrite the Nations' Cup matches from his own pocket and was more interested in his country reaching the 1998 World Cup finals.
Soccer is one of the few activities that unite Liberia, where almost seven years of civil war has killed well over 150,000 people.
